newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds embrace Q4 with record-year already set.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds embrace Q4 with record-year already set.

text.p: The Eurobond market started the fourth quarter in a buoyant mood on Tuesday, secure in the knowledge it has already notched up another record year.
"It's been a great year thus far, and we could see early funding for next year which will further boost supply," a syndicate manager at a U.S. bank said.
A syndicate manager at one European bank said, "Markets have surprised themselves with the level of issuance in recent months and we expect that supply to continue into the last quarter."
"The dollar will continue to lead all the other markets," said a new issues trader at another European bank.
An uncertainty for the Euromarket remains the direction of U.S. interest rates, after the U.S. Federal Reserve left rates unchanged at its late September FOMC meeting.
Most players now expected the Fed to raise rates by 25 basis points at the FOMC meeting in mid-November.
"A rise in rates is long-overdue...the Fed is clearly lagging behind market expectations," said one dealer.
While the dollar and the mark will remain the favoured currencies, syndicate managers said that, among the sectors, emerging market borrowers should prove buoyant.
International bonds worth $509 billion were launched in the nine months to the end of September, according to figures from Capital DATA Bondware.
The market has long since passed the record-breaking $464 billion recorded for all of 1995.

Dollars have made up the bulk of the volume -- $208 billion (41 percent of the total) up to the end of the third quarter this year versus $120 billion (34 percent) in the first nine months of last year.
Dealers also expected to see this year's stream of asset-backed bonds continue into the final quarter.
